facts.text: A Commander match of several games with three players
In the previous game, two of the three players lost (at different times) and the third player won

open_questions: How is 'lost first' decided when two players lose simultaneously (for example, both at the same state-based action check)? The user has not said.
What if a player who lost first was later shown to have lost at the same moment as another, or the game ends in a draw where no one lost first? The user says only that 103.1's draw rule applies.
Does the rule apply to Commander matches only or to every multiplayer match of several games? The user spoke of a three-player Commander match.
case.rule: In a multiplayer match of several games, if more than one player lost the previous game, the player who lost first in that game is the loser who chooses who takes the first turn. If the previous game was a draw, the draw rule of 103.1 applies unchanged.
applies_when: a multiplayer match of several games (such as a three-player Commander match) where the previous game was won by one player and more than one player lost it, or where the previous game was a draw

source.excerpt: In a match of several games, the loser of the previous game chooses who takes the first turn.

steps.conclusion: In a match of several games, 103.1 has the loser of the previous game choose who takes the first turn.

source.excerpt: Unlike two-player games, multiplayer games can continue after one or more players have left the game.

steps.conclusion: A multiplayer game can continue after a player has left it, so a multiplayer game can end with more than one player having lost, as F2 states.
When more than one player lost the previous game, the player who lost first in that game is the loser of the previous game for the purposes of 103.1 and chooses who takes the first turn.

source.excerpt: If the previous game was a draw, the player who made the choice in that game makes the choice in this game.

steps.conclusion: If the previous game was a draw, 103.1 already has the player who made the choice in that game make the choice in this game, and the proposed rule leaves this as it is.
